question.problem:
If $6a≡6b\,(\text{mod}\,8),$ then $3a≡3b\,(\text{mod}\,8)$ for any $a,b\in Z.$

A counterexample for the above statement would be a pair of integers $a$ and $b$ such that 

$$
{{field-1}}(\text{mod}\,8)\,\text{and}\,{{field-2}}(\text{mod}\,8).
$$
question.worked_solution:
By denoting $P(a)$ and $Q(a)$ as

- $P(a,b):\,6a≡6b\,(\text{mod}\,8)$

- $Q(a,b):\,3a≡3b\,(\text{mod}\,8)$

our statement can be written as

$$
∀a,b\in Z,\,P⇒Q.
$$

Since this statement is false, its negation is true.

A *counterexample* is a particular case that disproves the statement. Equivalently, it's a case that proves the negation is true.

The negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∀a,b\in Z,\,P⇒Q) & ≡\,∃a,b\in Z,\,¬(P⇒Q) \\  & ≡\,∃a,b\in Z,\,¬(¬P∨Q) \\  & ≡\,∃a,b\in Z,\,P∧¬Q \\  & ≡\,∃a,b\in Z,\,(6a≡6b\,(\text{mod}\,8))\,∧\,(3a≢3b\,(\text{mod}\,8)).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following:

A counterexample for the above statement would be a pair of integers $a$ and $b$ such that 

$$
6a≡6b\,(\text{mod}\,8)\,\text{and}\,3a≢3b\,(\text{mod}\,8).
$$
